title: Herdr Gives You Full Control Over Multiple AI Agents
description:
💬 Community: https://aiengineer.co
🔗 Free resources / skills: https://owainlewis.com/youtube

In this video I walk through Herdr, a terminal multiplexer built for AI developers, and show the exact setup I use to keep multiple coding agents organized instead of losing track of them across terminal tabs.

I cover the basic setup and key bindings, then get into the real value: using AI agents to control Herder itself, running a coordinator pattern where a single slash command spins up a new tab, branch, and worktree per ticket, and pushing that pattern to its extreme with milestones.

What you'll learn:
- How to install and navigate Herdr (spaces, agents, tabs, key bindings)
- How to point an agent at Herdr's own guide so it can manage your config for you
- The coordinator pattern: a `/ticket` command that creates a tab, branch, and worktree, then hands the ticket to a coding agent
- Running multiple tickets in parallel across separate tabs, each with its own agent
- Using a different coding agent (Neo) inside the same workflow for a bigger task, like adding Gemini provider support
- Taking the pattern further with milestones: handing a coordinator a whole batch of related tickets at once
- Honest trade-off: bigger tasks still need more review and more staying in the loop, even with this workflow
